countries.strDescriptionEN: The Campeonato Brasileiro de Futebol Feminino (Brazilian Women's National Championship) is an annual Brazilian women's club football tournament organized by the Confederação Brasileira de Futebol, or CBF. It is the country's premier women's football competition.

countries.strDescriptionEN:
The Campeonato Brasileiro Série D (English: Brazilian Championship Serie D), commonly known as the Série D or the Brazilian Série D to distinguish it from the Italian Serie D, is the fourth division of the Brazilian football league system, and was announced by the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) on 9 April 2008. The Campeonato Brasileiro Série D was formed from the split of the Série C, keeping its best 20 clubs and playing double round robin as does the top three divisions. The Série D keeps the same format of the older Série C, but with participation limited to 40 clubs recognized by the state federation. In 2016 the Série D was expanded to 68 clubs, but in 2022 it was reduced to 64 clubs.

The Série D format is a mixed system: the 64 clubs are divided in 8 groups organized regionally, playing in a round-robin format. The top teams qualify for playoffs and clubs that reach the semi-finals are promoted to Série C. Clubs qualify for the Série D by their performance at state championships — spots are given to the top clubs on those leagues that aren't at Série A, B or C — at state cups or relegation from Série C.

The Campeonato Acreano de Futebol is a competition organized by the Acre State Football Federation to compete for the state title among clubs from Acre. This tournament determines the state's places in open national competitions such as the Brazilian Football Championship - Series D, the Copa do Brasil, and the Copa Verde.

The Campeonato Alagoano de Futebol is a competition organized by the Alagoas Football Federation (FAF) to compete for the state title among clubs from Alagoas. Ten teams typically participate, and the champion and runner-up secure a spot in the following year's Copa do Nordeste and Copa do Brasil. The two highest-ranking teams not currently competing in any other national division also secure two spots in the following edition of the Brazilian Championship's Série D. The state's greatest rivalry is between CSA (Cento Sportivo Alagoano) and CRB (Clube de Regatas Brasil), the competition's biggest winners. Additionally, ASA (Associação Sportiva Arapiraquense) from Arapiraca is the main representative of the state's interior.

The Campeonato Amapaense de Futebol is an annual state-level football club competition organized by the Federação Amapaense de Futebol (FAF) and contested by clubs from Amapá, popularly nicknamed Amapazão. The competition is organized into two divisions called "Série A" and "Série B".
